title: Why Transformers — The Problems with RNNs

questions.question: A text model must distinguish “dog bites person” from “person bites dog.” What signal is essential?
options: Token order information in the model
A fixed-width summary of the sentence
Only the total number of tokens
A label attached to the final word
questions.explanation: The sentences use the same words but swap who acts on whom, so sequence order changes the event. A token-count summary loses that relation: both sentences have the same number of tokens and the same word multiset.

questions.question: Why can a recurrent model not compute hidden state hₜ before hₜ₋₁?
options: Each state uses the preceding hidden state
The input must first be converted to images
Each token requires a separate output classifier
Each state attends to all later positions
questions.explanation: The recurrence is hₜ = f(hₜ₋₁, xₜ), so state t cannot be evaluated until the prior state exists; sequence length therefore creates serial depth. A separate output classifier per token would not remove this dependency between hidden states.

questions.question: For token i, what does self-attention’s weighted-value sum compute?
options: A fixed average of the source sentence
A single score that ignores value vectors
A weighted sum of values from positions j
A recurrent state from the previous token only
questions.explanation: At position i, attention assigns weights aᵢⱼ to value vectors vⱼ and sums them, letting the query position select information from all positions. A fixed average gives every value equal weight and cannot express that learned relevance.

questions.question: At N = 1,024, what is the dependency depth of a balanced tree reduction compared with a serial scan?
options: 10 levels versus 1,024 serial steps
32 levels versus 512 serial steps
One level versus 1,024 serial steps
1,024 levels versus 10 serial steps
questions.explanation: A balanced binary reduction halves the remaining groups at each level, giving log₂(1,024) = 10 dependent combine levels; a serial recurrence waits through 1,024 steps. The one-level option confuses parallel execution with zero dependency depth.

questions.question: A service must process one token at a time with constant memory on an edge device. Which family fits the lesson’s selection guide?
options: A full sequence encoder-decoder
An RNN or state-space model
A global quadratic-attention stack
A full-attention transformer
questions.explanation: The guide reserves token-at-a-time, constant-memory streaming for RNNs or state-space models. Full attention retains interactions across positions, so its memory grows with sequence length; the full sequence encoder-decoder option does not supply the stated constant-memory property.

questions.question: A workload needs context beyond one million tokens and attention memory is the bottleneck. Which direction does the lesson recommend?
options: Linear attention, Mamba 2, or Hyena
A higher-resolution positional embedding table
A larger dense attention matrix
A fixed-width recurrent encoder summary
questions.explanation: The guide points to linear attention, Mamba 2, or Hyena when sequences exceed one million tokens and full-attention memory is the bottleneck. A larger dense attention matrix preserves the same quadratic memory scaling and worsens that constraint.
